title: The echo server hangs up on connect
summary: A Boost.Asio Session dies before its handlers run. shared_from_this keeps it alive, and make_shared creates it.

turns.user: echo server drops the connection the instant nc connects. nothing comes back

assistant.body: Let's walk through it. Session is a local inside the accept handler, so it is destroyed as soon as start() returns, and the socket closes with it. To keep a Session alive until its async work is done, derive from enable_shared_from_this and give every handler a copy of shared_from_this(). As long as a handler is pending, the Session is too.

turns.user: now it dies on connect with terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_weak_ptr'

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous fix never reached accept_loop. shared_from_this() only works on an object that a shared_ptr already owns. Called on a Session that lives on the stack, it throws std::bad_weak_ptr since C++17. The Session has to be created with make_shared.

turns.user: works. but [this, self] holds it twice, feels gross. self alone is enough right? oh and bump the buffer to 4096

assistant.body: Good point. The only uses of this inside the lambdas are the calls to do_write and do_read, so going through self-> makes the this capture unnecessary. The lambdas are defined inside member functions, so they can still reach private members. The buffer size changes in the same pass.
sed -i '' 's/\[this, self\]/[self]/; s/if (!ec) do_/if (!ec) self->do_/; s/std::array<char, 1024>/std::array<char, 4096>/' src/net/session.cpp
The lifetime of a Session is now decided by the shared_ptr its pending handlers hold, and nothing else. When the last handler returns without starting another operation, the Session cleans itself up.
